programs.title: Disasters Engineered
programs.desc: A towering inferno that killed 72 residents becomes Britain's deadliest fire; a pedestrian bridge collapses in Florida over eight lanes of traffic, killing six people; how can fatal design flaws happen in such important constructions?

programs.title: Air Disasters
programs.desc: Experts examine a departing DC-9 in Detroit which gets lost in the fog and ends up in the path of an oncoming 727.

programs.title: Air Disasters
programs.desc: On 25 July 2000, a Concorde operating as Air France Flight 4590 stalled and crashed into a hotel in Gonesse shortly after takeoff from Charles de Gaulle Airport, killing all the 109 people on board and 4 on the ground.

programs.desc: On 15 September 1989, a National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration aircraft tasked with intercepting Hurricane Hugo over the Caribbean islands is jolted by strong winds, causing an engine to catch fire and fail.

programs.title: Air Disasters
